rows.grounds: compound of strī (woman), vaśya (subjugation), and kṛt (making/causing)
genitive plural of priyaṅgu, naming the ritual substance
genitive singular of guggulu, naming the ritual substance
compound of bhūta (being/calamity), śānti (pacification), and da (giving)

items.question: Which specific ritual effects do priyaṅgu and guggulu produce when used as offerings?
premises: Priyaṅgu is associated with causing the subjugation of women.
Guggulu is associated with giving pacification of beings or calamities.
items.inference: Different ritual substances yield distinct powers, with priyaṅgu effecting subjugation and guggulu effecting pacification.
uncertainties: Whether bhūta in bhūta+śānti+daḥ refers specifically to malevolent beings or to calamities more generally is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Priyaṅgu brings about the subjugation of women, while guggulu brings pacification of harmful beings or disturbances.
